note: A NASCENT CAMPAIGN WORKTREE CAN BE RECYCLED OUT FROM UNDER THE SESSION THAT JUST TOOK IT, within seconds, and the symptom looks like a build failure. make worktree-take NAME=the-legend created the worktree at b7c97a4df and printed its normal success lines. A parallel session then ran worktree-take for another campaign, the pool recycler classified my seconds-old worktree as recyclable, and removed it. My backgrounded make prewarm died with cargo Error 101 after 19.9s, and the surviving directory held only a stray docs/timings.md that timed.sh had recreated. git worktree list no longer showed the-legend at all, while the branch campaign/the-legend still existed with no worktree. ROOT CAUSE is the same ancestry test The Beacon documented for notices: recyclability is tested by is-this-branch-merged, merged is tested by ancestry, and a freshly created branch tip EQUALS main, so it is trivially an ancestor of main and tests as merged the instant it is created. Measured: git rev-parse campaign/the-legend origin/main piped to uniq -c printed a single line with count 2, both b7c97a4df. THE TRAP is that the failure surfaces as a cargo error in an unrelated background job, and cargo then WALKS UP to the parent workspace from the emptied directory, so a follow-up cargo build --workspace run there exits 0 and looks like the tree is fine. It is answering about the main checkout, not the worktree. Discriminator: git rev-parse --show-toplevel returns the MAIN checkout path rather than the worktree path. WORKAROUND: make a commit on the campaign branch immediately after taking a worktree, before starting prewarm, so the tip stops equalling main and the recycler sees it as live. Discriminator for a real fix: a branch with a live worktree is live whatever the ancestry says, and a nascent branch is ahead 0 behind 0 while a genuinely merged one is ahead 0 behind more than 0.
